_notes: The BOOTSTRAP for the fleet config store, and nothing else reads it (docs/OPERATIONS.md, 'Where the config lives').
The live config is the store on the data volume: seed it from this file ONCE (bun runner/src/config-store.ts seed infra/fleet.example.json),
then edit it on the viewer's /config page or with the config-store CLI. The active config is operational state, never committed to git.
This file is a small, valid, representative roster that gives a fresh deployment a working board; it is not the fleet.
Fleet config 0.5. One concept, the JOB; one axis for evidence, the TIER; one axis for idle work, IDLE. Re-read every 60s.
roster.<name>.tier — how much evidence this model gets. THE only thing that sets a run count.
t0 trial     e90 x1, promotion HELD — it can never climb out on its own.
t1 standard  e90 x3, promotes to t2 on one counted e90 that reached level 5.
t2 long      e90 x3 + e360 x1.
Required on EVERY entry: the roster is a model CATALOG, so there is no
unscheduled entry left to make an exception for. objective and wikiCoords are REFUSED here —
steering is a campaign, which names the entry under `models` and owns its own task shape.
There is no per-entry override and no per-billing table: a bespoke volume is a NAMED tier in
runner/src/models.ts, reviewed like an episode id, never a number edited into one entry.
A t0 model that earns rung 1 KEEPS the witness (--status shows `t0*`): move it to t1 and it
promotes immediately on evidence it already has, with nothing re-run. Moving a model by hand is
always allowed and never records a promotion — `promoted` is only ever said of a climb.
roster.<name>.idle — what it does with an account once its tier is spent. Absent = none.
none        nothing. What a paid model wants, and the default so idle work is never bought by omission.
unlimited   one freeplay session at a time, unscored, with no episode wall-clock cap.
It remains one continuous character/session and ends only when its 20m idle watchdog fires.
roster.<name>.routing — which backend behind OpenRouter may serve this entry (docs/OPERATIONS.md).
A name, a list in preference order, or { order, sort, allowFallbacks, requireParameters }.
ABSENT = the model author's own provider, fallbacks OFF (operator decision 2026-09-16): a
third-party provider is a deliberate, named datapoint, never a silent fallback.
REFUSED on a claude-code/codex entry or a non-OpenRouter apiBase (Cerebras, LM Studio,
OpenCode Zen): one machine behind the endpoint, nothing to route between. policy.routing sets
the fleet default; an entry's own routing replaces it whole and is never merged with it.
billing — free or paid, derived (free slug / LAN / claude-code / allowlist -> free; else paid); roster.<name>.billing overrides.
Since 0.5 it says ONLY where a run may physically execute: the account class, and the rate-limit key.
It buys a model no runs and costs it none. Trial a paid model by giving it t0, not by editing a target.
accounts: three classes. An account belongs to exactly one; listing says who may SCHEDULE it, `enabled` says who HOLDS it.
pool  free models, in preference order. Never PROBE, never SMOKE*.
paid  paid picks land only here; with policy.paid present and this empty they are HELD, never spilled.
local a model on the operator's own hardware (isLocalBase) lands only here — the box serves one runner at a time.
A DISABLED pinned job may park on a listed account; an ENABLED one may not — THAT JOB is refused and left
disabled, named in --status and the fleet log, and the rest of the config stays in effect (item 66). Same for a
pinned campaign, and for two enabled pins on one account (the first in order keeps it). A LIVE run under a
refused pin is left alone — it finishes and does not respawn. Shape errors still
take the whole config down: a config that does not parse has no rest to keep.
roster entries: NO character name. The model names its own at createSession and the run records
what it chose; `character` is REFUSED by name here, like the other retired keys — a name in the
config is one the harness must keep valid and unique, and an invalid one takes the config down.
`race`/`class` are fixed dimensions and stay.
policy: only where runs execute and how many at once. maxConcurrent { <rate-limit key>: n } (concurrencyKeyOf);
paid { maxConcurrent } is the paid throttle. runsPerEpisode and extras are NOT 0.5 keys and are refused by name.
subscriptions — the Claude subscriptions the fleet may schedule on, as the NAMES of the env vars
holding their OAuth tokens; the tokens live in .env and never here. A subscription is a LANE, not a
model dimension: one roster entry per model however many accounts are behind it, because which
subscription paid says nothing about what a run measured. A claude-code run takes the first lane with
a session free and RECORDS the lane it billed, so the count survives a supervisor restart; a claude
pick with every lane full is held like any other cap. Absent = ["CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN"].
Rate-limit keys: a claude run counts against TWO and needs a free slot in BOTH — `claude-code`, every
Claude session in flight whoever pays, and `claude-code:<ENV NAME>`, that one subscription's. Every
lane has its own key, the default lane included, so the overall ceiling and a per-account limit are
never the same number. A key the config does not name is uncapped.
A queue job may add subscription: "<ENV NAME>" to pin itself to one subscription's usage window, and a
ROSTER ENTRY may do the same: roster.<name>.subscription pins that model's runs to one lane, and its pick is
HELD when that lane is busy rather than moved to another account. Normally absent. A name that is not in
policy.subscriptions refuses THAT ENTRY (named in --status, scheduled by nothing) and leaves the rest
of the config in effect.
The codex lane: a ChatGPT subscription is a lane too, and its variable names a logged-in CODEX_HOME
DIRECTORY rather than a token — list CODEX_HOME in subscriptions and cap `codex` at 1 (one live Codex
session per subscription) before adding a codex entry. It carries no `claude-code:` key of its own.
campaigns: probe campaigns, the third lane (see docs/EPISODES.md). { <name>: { enabled, models "all"|[refs],
runsPerCell, maxAttemptsPerCell?, cells [{ id, race?, class?, objective?, ... }], account?, objective?,
wikiCoords?, watchdogs?, maxToolCalls? } }. Every run is an unscored `probing` episode, so a
campaign is never re-armed by a harness bump — that is what separates a probe from an eval.
Precedence: episode-table defaults < campaign < cell. account set = PINNED (same rules as a
pinned job); absent = the policy schedules it, between the evals and the idle work.
Completion is DERIVED (cells x models x runsPerCell vs counted probe runs on disk), and a cell is
ABANDONED once it has had maxAttemptsPerCell launches (counted or not) — without that key a cell whose
launches keep failing is swept forever, since a failed launch is not a counted run. A finished
campaign gets enabled:false and KEEPS its results — see the /campaigns page.
queue: jobs { ref | [refs], episode e90|e360|freeplay, repeat n|"loop", enabled, account? }.
account set = PINNED to it (never policy-scheduled); absent = manual pool job, outranks the policy for a pool account.
A waiting manual job reserves the POOL only — the paid and local classes still pick (a226bbb).
preflight: the smoke gate the supervisor runs before spawning (docs/OPERATIONS.md); its accounts may not be in the pool or on a job.
